facts.content: Patient reports a "weird swelling" of the left elbow for approximately one week.
facts.source_text: • Chief Complaint: “Weird swelling” of left elbow for ~1 week.

facts.content: A 53-year-old man noticed a painless swelling over the left elbow while showering one week ago.
facts.source_text: 53-year-old man noticed painless swelling over left elbow while showering one week ago.

facts.content: The swelling is described as having mild warmth and a fluid-filled sensation.
facts.source_text: Describes mild warmth and fluid-filled sensation.

facts.content: The patient reports no preceding trauma.
The patient reports no prior episodes of similar swelling.
Full range of motion of the left elbow is preserved.
There is minimal tenderness adjacent to the swelling.
The tip of the left elbow is not painful.
The patient denies significant pain, erythema, or systemic symptoms.
facts.source_text: Denies significant pain, erythema, or systemic symptoms.

facts.content: Patient has osteoarthritis diagnosed by a prior GP.
Patient takes no routine medications.
Patient is allergic to peanuts; reaction not specified.
Patient has no known drug allergies.
Patient is unsure of family medical history.
Patient denies known rheumatoid conditions in the family.
facts.source_text: denies known rheumatoid conditions in family.

facts.content: Patient works a desk-based job.
Patient runs regularly two to three times per week.
Visible swelling is present over the posterior aspect of the left elbow.
facts.source_text: Visible swelling over posterior aspect of left elbow.

facts.content: The swollen area appears mildly warm relative to adjacent skin.
facts.source_text: Area appears mildly warm relative to adjacent skin.

facts.content: Full active range of motion of the left elbow is observed.
Minimal tenderness is noted adjacent to the swelling.
No marked erythema is reported.
Dry skin is observed over the tip of the left elbow.
facts.source_text: Dry skin over tip of left elbow.

facts.content: Swelling of the left elbow is present (musculoskeletal positive).
Patient reports no prior similar episodes (musculoskeletal negative).
Patient reports no limitation of movement (musculoskeletal negative).
Local warmth over the left elbow is present (skin positive).
Dryness is noted on the tip of the elbow (skin positive).
facts.source_text: dryness noted on tip of elbow (positive)

facts.content: Patient denies eczema elsewhere.
Patient reports no fever, chills, or malaise.
facts.source_text: No fever, chills, malaise (not specifically asked).

facts.content: Primary diagnosis is left olecranon bursitis.
Differential diagnosis includes septic arthritis or bursitis.
Differential diagnosis includes gouty tophus.
Differential diagnosis includes inflammatory arthropathy.
Ibuprofen 400 mg orally twice daily with food, OTC, advised to stop if heartburn or gastrointestinal symptoms occur.
facts.source_text: Ibuprofen 400 mg orally twice daily with food, OTC; stop if heartburn or gastrointestinal symptoms occur

facts.content: Ordered blood panel including inflammatory markers, infectious markers, rheumatologic antibodies, and serum uric acid.
facts.source_text: Order blood panel: inflammatory markers, infectious markers, rheumatologic antibodies, serum uric acid (gout screen).

facts.content: Blood test forms will be mailed to the patient with instructions.
facts.source_text: Blood test forms to be mailed to patient with instructions.

facts.content: Patient educated on red-flag symptoms and advised to seek urgent review if they occur.
facts.source_text: Educated patient on red-flag symptoms (increasing pain, redness, rapid swelling, systemic symptoms); advised to seek urgent review if these occur.

facts.content: Patient discharged home for self-care with NSAID.
Follow-up is scheduled approximately six days after blood draw to review results and reassess the elbow.
facts.source_text: Schedule follow-up (phone, video, or in-person per patient preference) approximately 6 days after blood draw to review results and reassess elbow.
